scenes.name: Delicious Vinyl: Tone Lōc, Young MC y The Pharcyde
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Los DJs de club Mike Ross y Matt Dike, inspirados por Def Jam, montaron su sello con los Dust Brothers y un sampler SP-12. Tone Lōc, un Crip de voz inconfundible, y Young MC, estudiante de economía de USC venido de Queens que les rapeó por teléfono, escribieron juntos «Wild Thing» (1988, sobre «Jamie’s Cryin’» de Van Halen, cuatro millones de copias gracias a KROQ y KDAY) y «Funky Cold Medina»; Young MC triunfó con «Bust a Move», con Flea al bajo. Un hip hop de radio en plena época gangsta, y luego The Pharcyde (Bootie Brown, Fatlip, Imani, Slimkid3, con J-Swift y J Dilla): Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde (1992) y «Passin’ Me By», los «Native Tongues bebés» de la Costa Oeste.

podcast.title: Absence from "Check Your Head" Production
podcast.body: The Dust Brothers, who were involved in *Paul's Boutique*, were not present to "take control" during the recording of *Check Your Head*, leaving the Beastie Boys to produce the album largely on their own. "The dust brothers weren't there to take control, so it was just the Beastie Boys doing their Beastie Boys thing."

xref.title: Lack of Label Supervision for "Check Your Head"
xref.body: During the creation of *Check Your Head*, the Beastie Boys experienced "almost any record company supervision," as they "d been written off by the labels, so they didn't take a lot of interest in the project." "Rick Rubin wasn't there to guide things. The dust brothers weren't there to take control, so it was just the Beastie Boys doing their Beastie Boys thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Lack of Record Label Supervision on Check Your Head
xref.body: During the recording of "Check Your Head," the band operated with almost no record company supervision because they had been "written off" by their label, which took little interest in the project. This allowed them complete creative freedom without figures like Rubin or The Dust Brothers guiding them. "They've been written off by the label, so they didn't take a lot of interest in the project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
